questions.prompt: Write a vector equation for the line through \((1,2,3)\) with direction vector \((4,-1,0)\).
questions.answer:
A line through point \(\mathbf p\) with direction \(\mathbf d\) has equation
\[
\mathbf r=\mathbf p+t\mathbf d,\qquad t\in\mathbb \(\mathbb R\).
\]
Here \(\mathbf p=(1,2,3)\) and \(\mathbf d=(4,-1,0)\), so
\[
\mathbf r=(1,2,3)+t(4,-1,0),\qquad t\in\mathbb \(\mathbb R\).
\]

questions.prompt: Does the point \((9,0,3)\) lie on the line \((x,y,z)=(1,2,3)+t(4,-1,0)\)?
questions.answer:
Set components equal. From the \(x\)-component:
\[
1+4t=9\quad\Rightarrow\quad 4t=8\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=2.
\]
Check the \(y\)-component with \(t=2\):
\[
2-t=2-2=0.
\]
Check the \(z\)-component:
\[
3+0t=3.
\]
All components match, so \((9,0,3)\) lies on the line.

questions.prompt: Find a direction vector for the line through \(A=(2,-1,4)\) and \(B=(5,3,0)\).
questions.answer:
A direction vector is the difference between two points on the line. Compute
\[
B-A=(5-2,3-(-1),0-4)=(3,4,-4).
\]
So a direction vector is \((3,4,-4)\). The opposite vector \((-3,-4,4)\) would also be valid.

questions.prompt: Find the intersection point of the line \((x,y,z)=(1,0,2)+t(2,1,-1)\) with the plane \(x+y+z=6\).
questions.answer:
Substitute the line components into the plane. From the line,
\[
x=1+2t,\qquad y=t,\qquad z=2-t.
\]
The plane equation becomes
\[
(1+2t)+t+(2-t)=6.
\]
Simplify:
\[
3+2t=6.
\]
So
\[
2t=3,\qquad t=\frac32.
\]
Substitute back into the line:
\[
(x,y,z)=\left(1+2\cdot\frac32,\frac32,2-\frac32\right)=\left(4,\frac32,\frac12\right).
\]
The intersection point is \(\left(4,\frac32,\frac12\right)\).
